ambiguities.text: The spec states weak subjectivity periods range from '~500 to ~3,500 epochs' without specifying exact boundary conditions for these ranges.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume these are approximate practical ranges based on mainnet validator counts (100k-800k validators) and average balances (32-34 ETH). Exact values depend on runtime state.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define how a node operator should obtain a trustworthy weak subjectivity checkpoint.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the checkpoint is obtained from a trusted source such as a block explorer, community checkpoint service, or another trusted node. The distribution mechanism is out of scope for this spec.

ambiguities.text: The compute_weak_subjectivity_period function uses Ether rather than Gwei 'to avoid overflow in uint64 arithmetic operations' but does not specify rounding behavior for the conversion.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume integer division (floor) is used when converting Gwei to Ether, which is standard practice in the consensus specs.

implicit_assumptions.description: The weak subjectivity checkpoint provided to the client is assumed to be from the canonical chain and not from an attacker-controlled fork.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the checkpoint itself is from an attacker's fork, the client will follow the wrong chain with no mechanism to detect this, permanently compromising the node.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker controlling less than 1/3 of the total stake cannot create conflicting finalized checkpoints.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If finalization can be achieved with less than 1/3 stake (due to a protocol bug), the economic security model breaks and long-range attacks become viable without sufficient slashing.

implicit_assumptions.description: Node operators will refresh their weak subjectivity checkpoints before the WS period expires.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Nodes running beyond the WS period without checkpoint refresh lose safety guarantees and become vulnerable to long-range attacks from historical validator keys.
